newsitem.title: USA: Conrail stock up on view of new deal terms.
newsitem.headline: Conrail stock up on view of new deal terms.

text.p: Shares of Conrail Inc traded higher in early afternoon on views that the railroad was on the verge of again revising terms of its proposed $8.5 billion transaction with CSX Corp.
The views came as Conrail was reviewing a $10 billion offer received last week from rival bidder Norfolk Southern Corp.
"The idea is to tighten up that spread (between the two offers) as best as they can," said one arbitrager.
Shares of Conrail gained one to 97-5/8.

Conrail rejected a previous offer from Norfolk Southern, contending that its merger agreement with CSX provided a better strategic fit. Conrail and CSX last week revised the terms of their cash-and-stock transaction to provide investors with more cash. But two days later, Norfolk Southern raised its all- cash offer to $110 per share from $100.
Some investors have reacted harshly to the CSX transaction, saying that Norfolk Southern's offer is better.
"Conrail's board has got to do some very serious thinking. I can't see them thumbing their nose at shareholders," said Charles Vincent at PNC Asset Management Group.

Traders and analysts speculated that CSX and Conrail may again boost the cash portion of the transaction. The latest terms call for CSX to pay $110 per share for 40 percent of Conrail's shares and exchange the rest for CSX stock at a ratio of 1.85619 CSX shares per Conrail share.
They said an increase in the cash portion is most likely because amending the deal to provide a more favorable exchange ratio would be dilutive to CSX.
A Conrail spokesman declined to comment on the board's meeting schedule. A CSX spokesman declined to comment.
